_about: laya_bpm = matras per minute, a typical practice tempo picked by ear from well-known renditions (not from a source). Taal is sourced per song. sa = the song's Sa as a MIDI note (61 = C♯, the room's default): the recordings' keys are not sourced, so every song starts on C♯; set it by ear on the tanpura and it can be written here. raga names a raga in ragas.json, which gives the backdrop. Western songs (genre 'western ·') carry chords, a metre and a comp pattern instead of a raga: the room loops the chords and a bass in the song's recorded key (approximate), with a drum kit or tabla; never the tune. 6/8 and 12/8 count eighths, so their bpm is eighths a minute.

teentaal.name: Teentaal
teentaal.theka: dha dhin dhin dha | dha dhin dhin dha | dha tin tin ta | ta dhin dhin dha
teentaal.prakar: dha dhin dhin-dhin dha-ti | dha dhin dhin-dhin dha-ti | dha tin tin-tin ta-ti | ta-ta dhin dhin-dhin dha-ti
teentaal.notes: UW writes matra 13 as 'na' (spoken 'na dhin dhin na' for euphony); 'ta' is the common form. Prakar = Digitabla's vilambit practice variation 1.

ektaal.name: Ektaal
ektaal.theka: dhin dhin | dhage ti-ra-ki-ta | tu na | kat ta | dhage ti-ra-ki-ta | dhi na
ektaal.prakar: dhin-.-.-.-.-.-te-te dhin | dha-.-.-.-ge-.-ge-ge ti-ra-ki-ta | tu na-.-.-.-na-.-na-na | kat ta | dha-.-.-.-ge-.-ge-ge ti-ra-ki-ta | dhin-.-.-.-.-.-te-te dha-.-.-.-dha-.-dha-dha
ektaal.notes: Prakar = Chhotelal Misra's vilambit ektaal theka (each matra in 4 pulses; written here on an 8-slot grid so 'tete' fits in one pulse). The last 'na' becomes 'dha'.

keherwa.name: Keherwa
keherwa.theka: dha ge na ti | na ka dhi na
keherwa.ghazal: dha dhin na ti | na ka dhin na
keherwa.prakar: dhin na-na tin ta | tin na-na dhin ta
keherwa.laggi: dha-ge ti-ra-ki-ta dhu-na ge-na | ta-ge ti-ra-ki-ta dhu-na ge-na
keherwa.notes: Ghazal/light form: 'ge' on matra 2 becomes an open 'dhin' (Digitabla variation 1, from Chhotelal Misra; 12notez says the dhin-for-ge swap is the usual ghazal accompaniment). Prakar = Carnatic Circle kism 2; laggi = Carnatic Circle laggi 3.

bhajani.name: Bhajani
bhajani.theka: dhin na-dhin .-dhin na | tin na-tin .-tin na
bhajani.variant: dhin dhin na-ke tin | tin tin na-ke dhin
bhajani.prakar: ti-ra-ki-ta na-dhin .-dhin na | dhin na-tin .-tin na
bhajani.laggi: dha-ti dha-dha dha-tin na-na | ta-ti dha-dha dha-dhin na-na
bhajani.notes: The lag is the point: the 2nd and 3rd dhin fall on the off-beat (half-way into matras 2 and 3), so it sounds 'dhin . na dhin . dhin na .' (kksongs: 'after the ta in matra 2 there is a dhin which starts half-way into the beat; the next dhin falls half-way into matra 3'; tablastudy writes 'dhin - nadhin - dhin na -'). Khali half is the same shape on closed tin (kksongs); tablastudy opens matra 5 with dhin. Variant = UW 'Bhajani keherwa' (Dhin dhin na - ke tin | tin tin na - ke dhin; placing na-ke inside matra 3 is my reading of their table). Prakar = tablastudy prakar 3; laggi = tablastudy 'Laggi 2'. Several sources note bhajani is not standardised and is often classed as a prakar of keherwa.
